propositions: Hypothesis: moving unchanged macOS pytest temporary trees to an APFS RAM disk reduces Gerrit Verify critical-path wall time and runner occupancy compared to runner.temp.

Result: all four independent treatment runs (31869753711, 31869919362, 31870391571, 31873067707) were slower than the exact no-RAM control 31868300174 (17m26s default, 20m36s job), ranging 18m26s–20m54s default, missing the predeclared 5% retention threshold of 16m33.7s default and 19m34.2s job.

Experiment rejected and reverted: the RAM-disk lifecycle was removed; both default and integration pytest tiers restored to runner.temp unchanged; no test selection, assertion, marker, worker count, timeout, coverage, platform cell, or collection changed.

Secondary defect discovered: workflow snapshot fixtures intentionally set read-only ownership; recursive basetemp cleanup raised PermissionError; fixed by restoring owner write permission before removal.
Tertiary defect discovered: nested pytest with cacheprovider enabled leaked .pytest_cache entries under outer no:cacheprovider; fixed by adding -p no:cacheprovider flag to nested subprocess.

All four workflow consumer tests (test_ci_workflow_parity, test_gate_step_tree_skew, test_extra_coverage_guard, test_worktree_python_pin) remained unchanged and passed; merged commit 7d908fbbc6da12f8e274b3ef1e3a2357377799ef contains no RAM-disk lifecycle and both basetemps under runner.temp.
